clue.text: Grass over after graduate mob runs riot

indicators.note: after says the letter for over follows the rest

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: running riot means going wild, so the letters of mob are thrown into disorder

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A rampaging crowd tramples the lawn, with a university graduate somewhere in the mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs riot' signals the anagram of the three letters given; 'after' sends the cricket over to the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is botanically a giant member of the grass family.

clue.text: A short hearing covering American nation

indicators.note: covering means the first pieces wrap around the next one
short means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing

explanation.surface: A brief court hearing involving an American citizen, with the country at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips the last letter of the hearing; 'covering' means the A plus clipped hearing wrap round the American abbreviation, which sits just after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a European country, so a straightforward example of a nation.

clue.text: Reveals feature of prison holding English

indicators.note: holding means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bars are on a prison's windows

explanation.surface: An exposé of a jail where an Englishman is detained.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare something is to uncover or expose it, a plain synonym of reveal.

clue.text: Convenient being one up for review around harbour

indicators.note: around says the reshuffled letters go round the other piece
something up for review gets reworked, so the letters of one up are reshuffled

parts.note: a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: A planning application for a harbour comes up for review, which proves handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for review' signals the anagram of 'one up', split in two; 'around' wraps that pair round the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed or suitable, a close synonym of convenient.

clue.text: Edges in wearing shoes, being careless

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: shod means wearing shoes
the lips of a cup or crater are its edges

explanation.surface: Someone shuffling in with their shoes on is being careless about the floors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges' looks like a verb of creeping, but it supplies LIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod describes slapdash, negligent work, so it fits a careless manner.

clue.text: Allowance from crown included in remit

indicators.note: included in says the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: to remit money is to send it
the crown of something is its tip or top

explanation.surface: A royal payment, part of an official's remit, as a regular allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular payment, such as a clergyman's salary or student grant.

clue.text: Divine liquid offered by church singers after promoting one

indicators.note: promoting moves the letter up to the front, as in a down entry raised to the top

I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sacred drink offered after a choir has been promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' moves the I of CHOIR to the front. In Greek myth, ichor is the fluid flowing in the gods' veins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor is the ethereal fluid of the gods of Greek myth, a liquid divine by nature.

clue.text: Shifting emphasis to keep time for companions on board

indicators.note: to keep means the shuffled letters hold the next piece inside
shifting the letters moves them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Moving the stress in a word while keeping the rhythm, for one's fellow sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifting' rearranges EMPHASIS; 'to keep' places T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipmates are fellow crew members aboard the same vessel.

clue.text: Natural love and caring, oddly

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Love and caring that come naturally, if a little oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown naturally, without synthetic chemicals.

clue.text: One problem splitting thread is such illumination

indicators.note: splitting says the pieces break into the other word

parts.note: a string is a thread
I is the Roman numeral for one
a plight is a predicament or problem

explanation.surface: A frayed thread turns out to be the trouble with this kind of lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Strip lighting is fluorescent tube lighting, a kind of illumination.

clue.text: Maintain power and propriety of manner

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
reserve is restraint or formality in manner

explanation.surface: Keeping one's authority while observing the proper decorum.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep it as it is, the sense of maintain.

clue.text: Empire builders taking some from answer

indicators.note: taking some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quiz cue: the empire builders, taking some of their reply from the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient people of Rome built one of history's great empires.

clue.text: Cake or meal found in 75% of France once

indicators.note: found in says this piece sits inside the next
three-quarters of a four-letter word keeps its first three letters

parts.note: Gaul is the old Roman name for the region that became France
tea is a light afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: A dessert choice or a full meal served across most of old France.
explanation.walkthrough: '75% of' keeps three of the four letters of the old name for France; 'found in' sets the meal inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, from the French word for cake.

clue.text: Comprehensive may be costly, needing tons for parking

indicators.note: needing says a letter swap is required
for says the new letter stands in place of the old one

parts.note: something expensive is costly
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A comprehensive car park may be expensive, needing tons of space for vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing ... for' swaps the P of EXPENSIVE for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Extensive coverage is wide-ranging and thorough, a synonym of comprehensive.

clue.text: Fool declines credit

parts.note: dips means falls or declines
tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A foolish person turns down an offer of credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is everyday British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipstick is informal slang for a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Fruit produced from two trees

parts.note: the first of the two trees is the pine, an evergreen conifer
the second of the two trees is the apple, grown in orchards

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit grown from two kinds of tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two trees' supplies both halves: PINE and APPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is a tropical fruit, a plain example of the category.

clue.text: Theory incorporating different line that's charted to a degree

definitions.text: line that's charted to a degree

indicators.note: incorporating says one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: an ism is a theory or doctrine
other means different, as in another way

explanation.surface: A theory that takes in a different line plotted on a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' looks like an anagram signal but is the synonym OTHER. 'to a degree' puns on degrees of temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotherm is a map line joining places of equal temperature, measured in degrees.

clue.text: Provide finance for track around the outskirts of Nimes

indicators.note: around says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a spoor is the track or trail of an animal

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Funding a racetrack on the edge of the French city of Nimes.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor an event is to fund it, usually for publicity.

clue.text: Skill in construction of 'Madonna carrying child'

indicators.note: carrying means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: the Madonna is the Virgin Mary
a son is a child

explanation.surface: The craft involved in building a statue of the Madonna carrying the infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madonna' looks like the singer, but it is the Virgin Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is the stonemason's craft of building with stone or brick.

clue.text: Settle comfortably in finest leather

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the following words

explanation.surface: Sinking cosily into the best leather armchair.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly, like a bird into its nest.

clue.text: Promise to go topless on a horse, and suddenly look cheerful

indicators.note: topless means losing the first letter, the top of a down entry

parts.note: to plight one's word is to promise it
a rider on a horse is said to be up

explanation.walkthrough: 'to go topless' drops the P of PLIGHT. A jockey 'up' is mounted on the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A face that lights up becomes suddenly bright with pleasure.

clue.text: Name inscribed in heart — a bit of a looker

indicators.note: inscribed in says the letter is written inside the other piece

parts.note: the core of something is its heart

explanation.surface: Carving a name into a heart for a rather attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a looker' sounds like an attractive person but means part of an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the clear front layer of the eye, part of whoever is looking.

clue.text: Demanded a second look ultimately with journalist

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter wanted another look before filing the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked can mean requested or required, as in asking a price.

clue.text: Ultra-modern sort of green gathering speed

indicators.note: gathering means taking the other piece in

parts.note: sage is a greyish-green colour
pace is speed

explanation.surface: A trendy shade of green that is quickly catching on.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-age describes something futuristic and highly advanced.

clue.text: English low-fat cream

parts.note: lite is the label spelling for reduced-fat products

explanation.surface: A tub of reduced-fat English dairy cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' looks like dairy but means the best.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its best members, the elite.

clue.text: Running through reason for deadlock

definitions.meaning: running someone through with a sword is sticking the point into them
an issue on which talks stall and agreement cannot be reached

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: running through with a blade is sticking its point in.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue blocking agreement in a negotiation causes stalemate, as does stabbing with a blade.

clue.text: Hover around poor diner being sociable

parts.note: to fly can mean to hover in the air

explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' signals the anagram of the diner; 'around' wraps the word for hover round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly person is warm and sociable towards others.

clue.text: Grant immunity to former partner, mostly unoccupied

parts.note: empty means unoccupied

explanation.surface: Letting off an ex-spouse because the house was mostly vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final Y from EMPTY.
